item.content:encoded: Forgive me for replying to a two year old comment, but I somehow just read this SCP for the first time, and I wanted to comment about precisely this. Methadone is for harm reduction, not detox. It actually has a much longer withdrawal period than heroin, so its primary use today is as a maintenance treatment for opiate addicts who just cannot seem to get and stay clean. Since anyone who becomes addicted to this drink can easily be kept away from it, methadone just doesn't make much sense. In fact, unless withdrawal from this is itself harmful (like withdrawal from long-term alcohol use can be), there isn't much reason to do any more than keep them contained and monitored until they've detoxed. Fortunately, the Foundation is pretty good at that sort of thing.

item.content:encoded:
948 seconds: D-Act consumes the last of SCP-209. Immediately stands and rushes to the body of D-Prey 1, begins clawing at the corpse with left hand, while maintaining hold of SCP-209 with the right.

954 seconds: Researchers determine that D-Act is attempting to refill SCP-209 with blood from the corpse of D-Prey 1. Per orders, one (1) security staff member enters and neutralizes D-Act, recovering SCP-209 still in its empty state.

The ending to me is also very effective. Three men dead, two killed by the other, the last one desperate to hold onto the power he held moments ago, terminated by security. Three souls go out, notes are taken, rinse and repeat.

item.content:encoded: Interesting. Were it not for the apparent lack of volition on the part of the Activator, this sounds like it could be an MC&D item. Sit back and enjoy a tasty scotch as you watch people die for your amusement. Makes we wonder if the Activator remembers their actions afterwards. Difficult to say given we only really see one trial involving them getting killed off afterwards. The extreme addiction would also seem to argue against MC&D, not because it's addictive, but having your customers groveling at your feet for another hit would be undignified.
